title: Start or Stop Anticoagulants Randomised Trial after Spontaneous Intracranial Haemorrhage
author: Rustam Al-Shahi Salman
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcw4ixgw

steps.title: Identify Potential Participants
steps.instruction: Identify adults (≥18 years) who have survived a spontaneous symptomatic intracranial haemorrhage (ICH, non-aneurysmal SAH, IVH, or SDH) and have atrial fibrillation/flutter (persistent or paroxysmal) with a CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥2.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the event occurred >24 hours prior to recruitment.
Verify that the haemorrhage was not due to trauma or haemorrhagic transformation of ischaemic stroke.
Confirm that the brain imaging used for the initial diagnosis is available.

steps.title: Screen for Exclusion Criteria
steps.instruction: Verify the participant does not meet any exclusion criteria before proceeding to consent.

substeps.instruction: Exclude if the patient has a prosthetic mechanical heart valve or severe native valve disease.
Exclude if the patient has previously undergone or intends to undergo left atrial appendage occlusion.
Exclude if the patient or doctor is already certain about whether to start full dose OAC.
Exclude if the patient is not registered with a GP, is lactose intolerant, or cannot understand spoken/written English.
Exclude if the patient has a life expectancy of less than one year.
For women of childbearing potential, perform a highly sensitive urine pregnancy test to confirm they are not pregnant.

steps.title: Obtain Informed Consent
steps.instruction: Provide the participant (or their personal/legal representative if the patient lacks capacity) with the Participant Information Leaflets (PIL) and Informed Consent Form (ICF).

substeps.instruction: Conduct an oral explanation covering all elements of the PIL and ICF.
Obtain a signed and dated ICF from the participant/representative and the investigator.
Provide the participant with a copy of the PIL and completed ICF.
Send a copy of the ICF to the Trial Coordinating Centre (TCC) via secure NHSmail.
Record the consent in the trial database to generate a unique trial identification number.

steps.title: Perform Brain MRI Sub-study
steps.instruction: For participants enrolled in the MRI sub-study, perform a brain MRI after the intracranial haemorrhage but before randomisation.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the MRI includes GRE T2*, T1, T2, FLAIR, and DWI sequences (and susceptibility-weighted imaging if available).
Send anonymised images in DICOM format to the TCC with an imaging transfer form.

steps.title: Collect Baseline Data and Randomise
steps.instruction: Collect all required baseline clinical data and submit the randomisation form via the secure web interface to the central randomisation service.

substeps.instruction: Collect co-morbidities, AF type, CHA2DS2-VASc and HAS-BLED scores, last serum creatinine, and two sedentary blood pressure readings.
Record the intended choice of intervention (DOAC or VKA) and comparator (antiplatelet or none) as decided by the physician.
Receive the treatment allocation and unique trial ID via email from the randomisation service.
Record the allocation in the participant's medical records and file the randomisation form in the Investigator Site File (ISF).

steps.title: Implement Treatment Allocation
steps.instruction: Prescribe and dispense the allocated treatment strategy within 24 hours of randomisation.

substeps.instruction: If allocated to 'Start OAC': Prescribe a full treatment dose of a DOAC (Apixaban, Rivaroxaban, Edoxaban, or Dabigatran) or a VKA (Warfarin, Acenocoumarol, or Phenindione) as chosen by the physician.
If allocated to 'Do not start OAC': Follow standard clinical practice, which may include antiplatelet drugs or no antithrombotic drugs.

steps.title: Manage Discharge and Initial Follow-up
steps.instruction: Complete the SoSTART discharge form upon the participant's release from the hospital or clinic.

substeps.instruction: Document the responsible consultant, all prescribed antithrombotic and antihypertensive drugs, and any outcomes occurring between randomisation and discharge.
Inform the participant's GP about the drugs prescribed on discharge.

steps.title: Conduct Annual Follow-up
steps.instruction: Perform annual assessments for at least one year after randomisation using questionnaires for the GP and the participant.

substeps.instruction: TCC sends GP questionnaire and ICF copy approximately four weeks before the randomisation anniversary.
Collect GP data on vital status, outcome events, three most recent BP measurements, and current repeat prescriptions.
Send participant questionnaire to collect data on outcome events, modified Rankin Scale score, and EQ-5D-5L quality of life.

steps.title: Monitor and Report Adverse Events
steps.instruction: Monitor participants for adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs) throughout the trial.

substeps.instruction: Assess each AE for seriousness, causality (unrelated, possibly related), severity (mild, moderate, severe), and expectedness (based on SPC).
Report all primary and secondary outcomes to the TCC.
Report SUSARs and SAEs (that are not outcomes or known ARs) to the ACCORD office within 24 hours via PDF email to safety@accord.scot or fax.
